items.label: FIGURE O.15
items.title: Positive relationship between income levels and GHG emissions (continued)

content.title_panel_c: c. High-income and upper-middle-income countries are responsible for 90 percent of historical emissions
content.data_trends: The chart shows a cumulative increase in CO2 emissions from 1850 to 2020. High-income countries represent the largest share of cumulative emissions, followed by upper-middle-income countries. Lower-middle-income and low-income countries represent a very small fraction of the total cumulative emissions.
content.sources: Panel c: PRIMAP-hist data from Gütschow, Pflüger, and Busch 2024.
content.notes: CO2e = carbon dioxide equivalent; GHG = greenhouse gas; CO2 emissions are cumulative in gigatons (gt) and do not include emissions from LULUCF. Country income groups are fixed at 2022 definitions.
